title: A national-security procurement prohibition can reduce direct exposure while supply-chain information remains fragmented
source_unit: GAO-26-108630 review of Section 889 foreign-sourced telecommunications and surveillance equipment prohibitions and implementation by DOD and GSA
geography: United States federal procurement and contractors; five identified Chinese telecommunications and surveillance companies and their affiliates

observations.period: Fiscal years 2016-2025; implementation review through March 2026

denominator.unit: Chinese companies named in Section 889 procurement prohibitions, with affiliates and subsidiaries included in the statutory scope

direct_obligation_trend.value: Federal obligations to the five identified companies declined after implementation in fiscal year 2019, with no spending in three fiscal years

contractor_representation.value: nearly 90% of companies with active federal contracts in fiscal year 2025 represented publicly that they did not use equipment from the five companies
contractor_representation.unit: share of active-contract companies as of March 2026

agency_controls.value: GSA and DOD had automated removal, search, and contractor-representation processes

information_sharing.value: GSA and DOD did not broadly share affiliate information and implementation insights with other agencies

security_endpoint.unit: avoided cyberattack, espionage, operational disruption, or strategic effect

observations.method: GAO analyzed procurement and System for Award Management data, reviewed DOD and GSA implementation processes, and interviewed agency officials; DOD and GSA together accounted for nearly two-thirds of fiscal year 2025 contract obligations.
observations.uncertainty: Public contractor representations do not independently verify equipment origin or affiliate relationships. The review focuses on DOD and GSA rather than every agency, and procurement reductions do not measure avoided threats, supply-chain substitution costs, or operational security.
observations.subgroup: DOD, GSA, other federal agencies, federal contractors, five named Chinese companies and affiliates, procurement officers, and supply-chain information systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower obligations may reflect market exit, substitution, waivers, or reporting changes rather than complete risk reduction. Sharing gaps may be addressable through existing mechanisms, and the absence of a reported incident is not evidence that the prohibition failed or succeeded.

related_sources.claim: GAO full report and accessible version for the Section 889 implementation review.

boundary: This record measures procurement prohibitions, contractor representations, agency implementation processes, and interagency information sharing. It does not establish verified equipment absence, avoided cyber or espionage events, operational continuity, supply-chain independence, or geopolitical leverage.
